evidence.source: 漢字簡化方案（1956）, reproduced at Wikisource
evidence.field: 第一表; 国务院决议
evidence.text: The 1956 scheme’s first table explicitly pairs 么 with 麽 as the simplified character; the decision says the first-table forms were to be used from 1 February 1956. This supports 么 as 麽’s standardized simplified form, independently of its older use as a graph variant of 幺.
evidence.title: 汉字简化方案

evidence.source: 汉典, 麼 entry quoting 說文解字
evidence.text: The entry quotes 說文: 細也。从幺麻聲。 It identifies 幺 as the semantic element for ‘fine/small’ and 麻 as the sound element. The same page labels the quotation 新附 in its reproduced text; this is a transmitted dictionary statement, not independent proof of actual ancient sound values or the graph’s earliest form.
evidence.title: 麼 mó、me、ma、má - 汉典

evidence.field: 國語辭典; 康熙字典
evidence.text: The entry gives a citation from 列子·汤问 using 么 in 么虫 with a gloss of small/fine, and quotes the Kangxi dictionary saying 么 is俗幺字 while warning that its use for 麼 is俗作么、誤. These attest distinct traditional lexicographic treatments: 么 as a vulgar/variant 幺 and a separate use written 么 for 麼. The page also cites a Tang poem by Li Zhong using final 么 in a question; dating that poem’s composition to Tang does not establish the date of its surviving manuscript spelling.
evidence.title: 麼 mó、me、ma、má - 汉典

evidence.field: 詳細解釋; 國語辭典
evidence.text: The entry records 麼/么 as a postposed element in words such as 什麼、怎麼、多麼, and as a sentence-final interrogative particle. It cites Li Zhong’s Tang poem 聽蟬寄朐山孫明府: 不知陶靖節，還動此心么？ and points to 列子 for the small-insect sense. This supports attestations of more than one use, but does not establish a direct semantic development from ‘small’ to interrogative suffix/particle.
evidence.title: 麼 mó、me、ma、má - 汉典

evidence.source: 山东大学 PDF, 汉语疑问代词演变的特殊规则
evidence.field: discussion of 何物/什物-derived interrogatives
evidence.text: The paper proposes a historical path in which 何物 (‘what thing’) became a word, then appeared as 何勿 and contracted to 勿; Tang–Five Dynasties forms included 没、摩、麽, with 么 becoming relatively fixed from the Song. This is a scholarly account of the spoken interrogative word and its spellings, separate from graphic formation. Its bibliographic discussion points to earlier scholarship; it does not by itself settle all competing derivations.
evidence.title: 汉语疑问代词演变的特殊规则

gaps: No inspected paleographic source established the earliest attested forms or graphic evolution of 么/幺, and the proposed silk-thread depiction for 幺 was not externally verified here.
The dossier’s claim that 么 is a variant of 幺 is consistent with Han Dian’s quoted Kangxi entry, but its exact chronology and graph relationship remain unsupported by inspected paleographic evidence.

The semantic link between the old ‘small/fine’ sense and the interrogative suffix/particle is not established by the inspected sources. The 何物 contraction account is a separate proposed history of the spoken interrogative word and its spellings; source disagreement involving 無 or 物 remains unresolved.

No early, directly inspected primary corpus examples were obtained to date the first particle uses; the Tang poem citation is reported by a modern dictionary and cannot establish manuscript spelling chronology.

Current kMandarin readings for all four characters could not be verified: local extract lacks these rows, and official individual Unihan pages were inaccessible. No phonetic-component reading claim is made.
No sufficiently clear reuse terms for Han Dian were verified; no local extract is recommended.
